_note: Inputs to the boss balance simulation (tests/bots/BossBalance.gd). Everything here is an ASSUMPTION about how people play, not measured data: replace the numbers with real playtest figures when they exist and re-run `godot --headless --path . tests/bots/BossBalanceRunner.tscn`. 'model' says how a simulated person behaves; 'archetypes' are the kinds of player; 'loadouts' are what they bring; 'targets' are the win-rate bands the boss is tuned to (checked by tests/unit/test_boss_balance.gd).

model._recall: A player's `recall` is the chance they know the answer when they first see a plain clue. After a miss they get another look: the chance rises by this fraction of what is missing (the reworded phase-1 clue helps more than a plain retry).
model._phase: Phase 2 asks for the OPPOSITE of a clue, which takes an extra mental step: recall is multiplied by this. Phase 3 wants an archaic spelling: of the players who know the word, this fraction type the archaic form straight away; the rest type the modern spelling (accepted, but worth the boss's exact_match penalty).
model._time: A player's `speed` is the typical fraction of the clue's clock they use to answer; harder prompts take longer (phase multipliers) and each answer varies (log-normal, this spread). Running out of clock is a miss.

loadouts._note: arrival_hp is the fraction of max HP the player has when they reach the boss (a floor's fights leave them hurt). `tomes` go through the real LexiconEffects, so 'geared' is a Lv 30 player who bought Vitality, Ward and Might.

targets._note: Win-rate bands [low, high] for the GEARED loadout (a Lv 30 player with three good tomes: the player the boss is meant for), by depth. The design intent: the first boss (depth 5) is a coin-flip for an average player and a fair test for a strong one; deeper bosses get harder, but gently, so every fifth floor is still a fight you can win rather than a wall. Bands are 14-17 points wide, held at both the smallest and the largest supported grid (a bigger grid gives the boss a little more HP), with the boss's round clock bonus in place. 'bare' (no tomes) is only floor-checked: a player with no gear should still have a real chance if they are skilled.
